metaTitle: Shimuja Ramen Case Study: 15.4M Views | Button Up Media
metaDescription: How Button Up Media's social media marketing helped Shimuja Ramen reach 15.4M views while the shop moved from Southwest Ranches to downtown Miami.
ldHeadline: Shimuja Ramen: 15.4M social media views for a downtown Miami ramen shop
answer: Shimuja Ramen serves at Julia & Henry's food hall in downtown Miami. Our short videos put the ramen first and reached 15.4M social views.
timeframe: About 4 years, by Chef Kei's count

metrics.label: Social media views
metrics.meaning: Each view is a chance for someone nearby to find the shop and come try a bowl.

metrics.label: Working together
metrics.meaning: By Chef Kei's count. Social media pays off when it runs month after month, not in one short burst.

metrics.label: Homes so far
metrics.meaning: Southwest Ranches, pop-ups at Baby Jane in Brickell and in Sunset Harbour, and now Julia & Henry's.

paragraphs: Shimuja has moved more than once. It started in Southwest Ranches in Broward, ran pop-ups at Baby Jane in Brickell and at Sunset Harbour in Miami Beach, and now serves ramen at Julia & Henry's in downtown Miami.
Every move means telling regulars where to find you and winning over a new neighborhood.

points: Chef Kei sees it at the counter: in his words, a lot of the customers who come try his ramen come directly from our social media marketing.

quote.text: I can see a lot of customers that come try my ramen come directly from the social media marketing Button Up has done for me, and I'm very grateful for what they've done for Shimuja in the 4 years we've been working with them.
